rows.name: a tool's result is cut at MAX_RESULT characters, saying so
AGENT_ISSUER must be one of the origins served
an alias serves everything, names MCP resources as reached, keeps the issuer, and sends browser pages to the public URL
MCP clients sign in with OAuth: registration, consent, PKCE, rotating refresh tokens, revocation
the hosted MCP endpoint runs the CLI's tools as the caller, and reads no files or environment
the OpenAI apps domain challenge is served as plain text from AGENT_OPENAI_APPS_CHALLENGE
the application's own connection still answers a replay gap with 409 unless it asks for a snapshot, as relays that do not read snapshots expect
a run for an agent whose tools need its application is refused while none is connected, after a short wait for one reconnecting
the application's ready event carries the hash of the tools it last declared, so an SDK reconfigures only on a change; a run's outcome carries its usage
one application serves an agent's tools at a time: another connection is refused unless it takes over, and the replaced one is told why
a connection that holds an agent but no longer answers (half-open) is replaced without a takeover
an agent takes builtins without a definition: at creation, by upsert and by configuration, and only from its tenant
web_fetch reads public pages as text, from the model and codemode, and never reaches inside
web_fetch refuses internal addresses when nothing is allowed
an agent schedules, lists and cancels its own wake-ups, and wakes up
a schedule of an agent at its spend limit records the 402 and moves to its next occurrence instead of retrying
codemode runs on V8 for every tenant, and the limits API refuses an engine
an upsert's mcpServers are part of its configuration and configHash
a stateless run calls its own MCP servers
an agent without a definition has MCP servers of its own, called with identity tokens that name it and no definition
an agent's or run's own MCP servers take no credentials, and an agent from a definition takes none of its own
tool lists refresh when the server says they changed, and edits keep sealed credentials
applying a definition lists its servers afresh: a tool added without a list_changed notice reaches the agent at once
an agent shows every tool source and what its model gets, connecting to MCP servers only when asked
MCP servers must be on public addresses, checked when saved and again when connecting
a server that only speaks the older SSE transport is reached through it
tool servers get the model's call id, codemode's too, and the actor; their progress reaches the event stream
a burst of progress is coalesced per call: the stream gets the first, then the latest of each window, and the last before the result
a call that keeps reporting progress outlasts its timeout, which limits only silence
an MCP server's tools reach the model and codemode; its credentials are sealed and go only to it
a tool source that cannot be listed is named in every run's outcome
an MCP server is listed when its definition is saved: refused credentials are a 400 then, and what it lists or why it could not is in the answer
a direct tool's large result is cut for the model, as codemode's output is, with the whole of it saved to the workspace
history and forks keep capped tool details and deduplicated prompts without changing model content
every tool call carries a stable idempotency key: MCP servers in _meta, OpenAPI operations as an Idempotency-Key header
calls whose ids repeat across turns (as providers that number calls per response give them) get keys of their own
a run's outcome lists its tool calls, those from code too, by name and id with how each went, the first 100 only
an attached tool's own timeoutMs bounds its call; progress extends it; a timeout is an unknown outcome, in the run's outcome too
the console registers the tools with the browser, runs them as the signed-in tenant, and unregisters on sign-out
in the console, the tools authenticate with the session cookie and the console header, not a key
